name: The Big Picture Story Bible
description:
The Big Picture Story Bible — God's Great Story for Every Child

Everyone loves a good story.

Children especially. They are drawn instinctively to stories — to the sweep of a great narrative, to characters they can follow and care about, to a plot that builds toward something meaningful and true. And the greatest story ever told — the one that is more real, more epic, and more personally significant than any other — is the story of the Bible.

But here is what children — and many adults — often miss: the Bible is not a collection of separate stories. It is one story. A single, unified, magnificent narrative that runs from the very first words of Genesis to the final vision of Revelation — the true account of God's unstoppable love for the world he made and the people he created to know him.

The Big Picture Story Bible by David Helm is designed to help children see that big picture — to follow the whole storyline of God's Word from beginning to end, and to understand that every part of it connects, every part of it matters, and every part of it is ultimately about the same thing: God's great love and his great plan of redemption through Jesus Christ.

More Than Bible Stories — The Bible Story

The way we tell children the Bible matters enormously. When Bible stories are presented as separate, disconnected moral tales — David and Goliath as a lesson about courage, Noah as a lesson about obedience, Daniel as a lesson about faith — children miss the most important thing about them. They miss the fact that these are not independent stories with individual morals. They are chapters in one great story — each one pointing forward to Jesus, each one making more sense in light of what he came to do.

The Big Picture Story Bible takes a different approach. David Helm takes children on a journey through the whole storyline of God's Word — showing how the Old Testament sets the stage for what Jesus will do, how the New Testament reveals what God has been planning all along, and how the entire Bible from Genesis to Revelation is the story of a God who loves his world and will stop at nothing to rescue it.

This whole-Bible approach does not just give children more Bible knowledge. It gives them a framework for understanding everything — a big picture within which every individual story, every promise, every prophecy, and every person finds its proper place and meaning.

What Makes This Bible Special

A Whole-Bible Narrative Rather than selecting favourite stories and presenting them in isolation, The Big Picture Story Bible takes children through the complete arc of Scripture — from creation and the fall, through the story of Israel and the coming of Christ, to the resurrection and the hope of the new creation. Children who grow up with this Bible will have a genuinely biblical understanding of how God's story fits together.

Written for Children David Helm writes with the clarity, warmth, and narrative engagement that children need and love. The language is accessible without being shallow, the pacing is engaging without being rushed, and the storytelling is vivid without losing the substance of what Scripture actually teaches.

Fully Illustrated The print edition of The Big Picture Story Bible is fully illustrated — bringing the world of Scripture to life visually for young readers and helping children engage with the story at a deeper level. The illustrations are not merely decorative but are carefully crafted to support and enrich the narrative.

Gospel-Centred Throughout From beginning to end, The Big Picture Story Bible keeps the gospel at the centre of the story it tells. Children are not left with the impression that the Bible is primarily about how to behave well. They are shown that the Bible is primarily about what God has done — about his grace, his rescue, his love, and his Son.

What This Book Will Help Your Child Do

  • Understand the Bible as one unified story rather than a collection of disconnected tales
  • Follow the whole narrative of Scripture from Genesis to Revelation with clarity and engagement
  • See how every part of the Bible connects to the central story of God's redemption through Jesus Christ
  • Develop a genuine love for God's Word from the earliest years of life
  • Build a biblical framework for understanding God, the world, themselves, and the gospel
  • Engage with the Bible in a way that goes deeper than surface-level moral lessons
  • Be prepared for a lifetime of faithful Bible reading by understanding the big picture from the start

Who Should Use This Book?

The Big Picture Story Bible is ideal for:

  • Parents who want to read the Bible with their young children in a way that is engaging, accessible, and genuinely faithful to the whole of Scripture
  • Families looking for a resource for family devotions that helps children understand the Bible as one connected story
  • Sunday school teachers and children's ministry workers wanting a whole-Bible narrative resource for their classes
  • Church libraries and resource centres serving families with young children
  • Grandparents who want to give a gift that will shape a grandchild's understanding of the Bible from an early age
  • New Christian parents who want to introduce their children to the Bible in the most faithful and engaging way possible
  • Any family in India wanting to ground their children in the Word of God from childhood — in a format that is both theologically sound and genuinely enjoyable for young readers

About the Author

David Helm is a pastor at Holy Trinity Church in Chicago and the chairman of the Charles Simeon Trust, which works to promote faithful biblical preaching. He is the author of several widely used resources including a one-to-one Bible reading handbook and a preaching commentary on 1 and 2 Peter. In The Big Picture Story Bible, he brings his commitment to faithful, whole-Bible engagement to the youngest readers — helping children encounter the God of Scripture through the story that Scripture tells from beginning to end.

A Gift That Lasts a Lifetime

Of all the things a parent or grandparent can give a child, few are more valuable than a genuine understanding of and love for God's Word. The Big Picture Story Bible is not just a children's book that will be read for a few years and then outgrown. It is an investment in a child's spiritual foundation — a resource that shapes the way they understand God, the world, and themselves for the rest of their lives.

Children who grow up understanding that the Bible tells one great story — and that they are invited into that story through faith in the one it is ultimately all about — are children who are being given something of immeasurable and eternal worth.

The Big Picture Story Bible is a beautiful, faithful, and genuinely engaging way to give them exactly that.

name: Jesus Moments: David- Finding Jesus in the Story of David
description:
Jesus Moments: David — Discovering How David Points to Jesus

Every story in the Old Testament is pointing somewhere.

Behind the battles and the poetry, behind the shepherd boy and the giant, behind the king who danced before the ark and the man after God's own heart — there is a thread running through every moment of David's story that leads, unmistakably and gloriously, to Jesus.

Jesus Moments: David by award-winning author Alison Mitchell is a beautifully illustrated Old Testament storybook designed to help children aged 4 to 7 begin to see that thread — to discover the moments in David's story when he is a little bit like Jesus, and to start developing the most important reading skill a young Christian can have: the ability to see the whole Bible as one story about Jesus.

This is the first book in the Jesus Moments series — a collection of storybooks that look at how Old Testament characters point to the one they were always anticipating.

More Than a Story About David

Most children know something about David. The shepherd boy. The giant-killer. The king who played the harp and wrote the psalms. The man after God's own heart.

But David's story is more than a collection of exciting episodes and moral examples. It is a story that was always pointing forward — to a greater shepherd, a greater king, a greater deliverer, and a greater man after God's own heart. A story that finds its fullest meaning not in David himself but in the one David was always, in so many ways, a picture of.

Jesus Moments: David helps young children begin to see this connection — not in a way that bypasses the genuine richness of David's own story, but in a way that opens up its deepest meaning by showing where it ultimately leads.

This is the kind of Bible reading that shapes a child's entire relationship with Scripture — giving them not just knowledge of individual stories but a framework for understanding how every part of the Bible connects to Jesus.

How the Book Works

One of the most creative and genuinely effective features of Jesus Moments: David is its interactive design. Throughout the book, moments in David's story when he is a little bit like Jesus are signposted with symbols that children are invited to spot.

This simple but powerful device does several things simultaneously:

  • It makes the reading experience actively engaging — children are not just listening or looking at pictures but searching, finding, and making connections
  • It trains children in a genuinely biblical reading skill — the ability to notice how the Old Testament anticipates and points forward to Jesus
  • It makes the typological connections between David and Jesus concrete, memorable, and personally discovered rather than simply told
  • It creates natural opportunities for conversation between parent and child about what the connections mean and why they matter

By the time children have worked through the book, they have not just heard stories about David. They have begun to develop the habit of reading the Old Testament with eyes that are looking for Jesus — the most important reading habit any Christian can cultivate.

What Children Will Discover

As they journey through the key moments of David's story — from his anointing as a young shepherd to his reign as king of Israel — children will begin to notice the remarkable ways in which David foreshadows Jesus:

  • David the shepherd who cares for and protects his flock — pointing to Jesus the Good Shepherd who lays down his life for his sheep
  • David the unlikely, overlooked youngest son chosen and anointed by God — pointing to Jesus the one whom the world rejected but God exalted
  • David the deliverer who defeated the enemy that his people could not overcome — pointing to Jesus who defeated sin and death on behalf of all who belong to him
  • David the king after God's own heart who established his throne in Jerusalem — pointing to Jesus the eternal King whose kingdom will never end
  • David the one who brought blessing to his people through his victories — pointing to Jesus through whom every spiritual blessing flows to all who are in him

Each of these connections is handled with the care and simplicity that young children need — accessible enough for a 4-year-old to enjoy with a parent, rich enough for a 7-year-old to genuinely engage with and begin to understand.

What This Book Will Help Your Child Do

  • Begin to understand the relationship between the Old and New Testaments — that the Old Testament was always pointing to Jesus
  • Develop the habit of reading the Bible with eyes that look for Jesus in every part of Scripture
  • Encounter the story of David in its full richness — as both a genuinely exciting narrative and a profound pointer to Christ
  • Build the biblical literacy and theological framework that will serve them for a lifetime of Scripture reading
  • Engage actively and imaginatively with the Bible through the symbol-spotting interactive feature that makes every page an adventure
  • Develop confidence in their ability to make connections across Scripture — between the Old Testament stories they know and the Jesus they are coming to love

Who Should Use This Book?

Jesus Moments: David is ideal for:

  • Parents of children aged 4 to 7 who want to teach their children to read the Bible as one unified story about Jesus from the very beginning
  • Grandparents looking for a meaningful, gospel-centred gift that will shape a grandchild's understanding of Scripture
  • Home-educating families wanting a high-quality Bible storybook that combines narrative engagement with genuine theological depth
  • Sunday school teachers and children's ministry workers looking for a resource that helps children understand the relationship between the Old and New Testaments
  • Churches wanting to resource parents with practical, accessible tools for gospel-centred Bible teaching at home
  • Any family in India wanting to give their young children a beautiful, theologically rich introduction to the story of David and its connection to Jesus

About the Author

Alison Mitchell is an award-winning children's author whose books have helped thousands of children encounter the Bible in ways that are both genuinely engaging and theologically faithful. She is the author of the beloved Jesus and the Lions' Den and The One O'Clock Miracle — both of which have won awards for their quality and gospel-centred approach to children's Bible storytelling. In Jesus Moments: David, she brings the same gifts of clear, warm, child-friendly writing and deep biblical faithfulness to the challenge of helping the youngest readers discover how the Old Testament points to Jesus.

About the Jesus Moments Series

Jesus Moments: David is the first book in the Jesus Moments series — a collection of beautifully illustrated Old Testament storybooks that look at how key Old Testament characters point to Jesus. Each book in the series is designed to help children aged 4 to 7 develop the skills and instincts needed to read the whole Bible as the one great story it truly is — the story of Jesus, told from Genesis to Revelation.

The series is built on the conviction that children are never too young to begin seeing the connections between the Testaments — and that the earlier they develop this skill, the richer and more faithful their engagement with Scripture will be throughout their entire lives.

A Gift That Shapes a Lifetime of Bible Reading

There is a way of reading the Bible that misses its deepest meaning — that reads the Old Testament as a collection of moral tales and exciting adventures without ever seeing the one they are all pointing to. And there is a way of reading the Bible that sees everything clearly — that recognises Jesus on every page, that understands how promise and fulfilment connect, and that finds in the whole of Scripture one magnificent, unified, Christ-centred story.

Jesus Moments: David is an investment in giving your child the second way of reading — from the very earliest years of their life.

It is one of the most valuable gifts any parent, grandparent, or teacher can give to a young child who is just beginning their journey with Scripture.

name: Jesus Moments: Moses - Finding Jesus in the Story of Moses
description:
Jesus Moments: Moses — Discovering How Moses Points to Jesus

The story of Moses is one of the most dramatic and beloved in all of Scripture.

A baby hidden in a basket on the Nile. A burning bush in the desert. Ten plagues and a mighty deliverance. The parting of the Red Sea. Forty years in the wilderness. The giving of the law on Mount Sinai. A leader who brought God's people from slavery to the edge of the promised land.

It is a story of extraordinary power, breathtaking miracles, and remarkable faith. But like every story in the Old Testament, it is also pointing somewhere. Running through every moment of Moses' life — through every rescue, every act of deliverance, every encounter with God — is a thread that leads forward to the one Moses himself was always anticipating.

Jesus said so himself: "Moses wrote about me."

Jesus Moments: Moses by award-winning author Alison Mitchell is a beautifully illustrated Old Testament storybook that helps children aged 4 to 7 begin to see that thread — to discover the moments in Moses' story when something in it is a little bit like Jesus, and to take another step in developing the most important reading skill a young Christian can have: the ability to see the whole Bible as one story about Jesus.

This is the second book in the celebrated Jesus Moments series.

Moses and Jesus — A Connection Written Into the Story

The connection between Moses and Jesus is not something that has to be forced onto the text of Scripture. It is woven into it — explicitly acknowledged by Jesus himself, developed by the New Testament writers, and visible to any reader who knows what to look for.

Moses was the great deliverer — the one through whom God rescued his people from slavery in Egypt. Jesus is the greater deliverer — the one through whom God rescues his people from the far deeper slavery of sin and death.

Moses was the mediator of the old covenant — the one who stood between God and his people, receiving the law on their behalf and interceding for them when they failed. Jesus is the mediator of the new covenant — the one who stands between God and his people not merely to pass on commands but to bear their punishment and secure their forgiveness.

Moses led God's people through the waters and into the wilderness — sustaining them with bread from heaven and water from the rock. Jesus leads his people through death and into new life — sustaining them with himself as the true bread from heaven and the living water that satisfies forever.

Moses saw the promised land from a distance but could not enter it himself. Jesus has not only entered the true promised land but has opened the way for all his people to follow him in.

Jesus Moments: Moses helps children aged 4 to 7 begin to see these connections — not in an abstract or theological way, but in the concrete, visual, interactive, story-by-story way that young children can genuinely grasp and delight in.

How the Book Works

Like the first book in the Jesus Moments series, Jesus Moments: Moses uses a simple but highly effective interactive device: throughout the book, moments when something in Moses' story is a little bit like Jesus are signposted with symbols that children are invited to spot.

This symbol-spotting feature transforms the reading experience from passive listening to active, engaged discovery — making children genuine participants in the process of connecting Moses' story to Jesus rather than simply recipients of information.

The benefits of this approach are multiple and significant:

  • Children develop the habit of reading the Old Testament with eyes that look for Jesus — the single most important hermeneutical skill a young Bible reader can cultivate
  • The connections between Moses and Jesus become personally discovered rather than simply told — which makes them far more memorable and far more meaningful
  • The interactive element makes the book genuinely enjoyable to read repeatedly — and each re-reading deepens the child's understanding and strengthens the connections they have begun to make
  • The symbol-spotting creates natural, organic conversation opportunities between parent and child about what the connections mean and why they matter

By the time children have worked through the book, they have not just heard about Moses. They have taken a significant step toward reading the whole Old Testament the way Jesus himself said it should be read — as a book that is fundamentally about him.

What Children Will Discover

As they journey through the key moments of Moses' extraordinary story, children will begin to notice the remarkable ways in which Moses and the events of his life foreshadow Jesus:

  • The baby Moses hidden in a basket to save his life from a murderous king — pointing to the baby Jesus hidden in Egypt to save his life from a murderous king
  • Moses leaving the comfort and privilege of Pharaoh's palace to identify with his suffering people — pointing to Jesus leaving the glory of heaven to enter into the suffering of humanity
  • Moses the deliverer who brought his people out of slavery through the blood of the Passover lamb — pointing to Jesus the Lamb of God whose blood delivers his people from the slavery of sin
  • Moses leading his people through the waters of the Red Sea to safety — pointing to baptism and the new life that comes through dying and rising with Christ
  • Moses the mediator who stood between God and his sinful people and interceded for them — pointing to Jesus the one mediator between God and humanity who intercedes for his people forever
  • Moses giving God's people the bread from heaven in the wilderness — pointing to Jesus who declared himself to be the true bread from heaven that gives eternal life

Each connection is presented with the warmth, clarity, and child-friendly accessibility that Alison Mitchell brings to everything she writes — making deep biblical truth genuinely available to the youngest readers.

What This Book Will Help Your Child Do

  • Continue developing the skill of reading the Old Testament as a story that points to Jesus — building on what they began in the first Jesus Moments book
  • Discover the remarkable and specific ways in which Moses' life and ministry foreshadow the person and work of Jesus Christ
  • Understand more clearly the relationship between the Old and New Testaments — that the Old was always preparing for and pointing to the New
  • Engage actively and imaginatively with the Bible through the symbol-spotting interactive feature that makes every reading experience an adventure
  • Build the biblical literacy and theological framework that will shape their entire lifetime of Scripture reading
  • Develop a growing love for the whole Bible — Old Testament and New Testament together — as the one great story of God's rescue of his people through Jesus

Who Should Use This Book?

Jesus Moments: Moses is ideal for:

  • Parents of children aged 4 to 7 who want to help their children develop the skill of reading the Bible as one unified story about Jesus from the earliest years
  • Families who have already read Jesus Moments: David and want to continue the series with their children
  • Grandparents looking for a meaningful, gospel-centred gift that builds on and deepens a grandchild's understanding of how the Old Testament connects to Jesus
  • Home-educating families wanting a high-quality Bible storybook for their curriculum that combines genuine narrative engagement with deep theological faithfulness
  • Sunday school teachers and children's ministry workers wanting a resource that helps young children understand the typological connections between Moses and Jesus
  • Churches wanting to resource families with beautiful, accessible, gospel-centred Bible storybooks for use at home
  • Any family in India wanting to give their young children a rich, illustrated introduction to the story of Moses and its profound connections to the story of Jesus

About the Author

Alison Mitchell is an award-winning children's author whose books have introduced thousands of children to the Bible in ways that are both genuinely engaging and deeply theologically faithful. She is the celebrated author of Jesus and the Lions' Den and The One O'Clock Miracle — both widely praised for their quality and their gospel-centred approach to children's Bible storytelling.

In the Jesus Moments series, Mitchell brings her distinctive gifts of warm, accessible, child-friendly writing and careful biblical thinking to the specific challenge of helping the youngest readers discover how the Old Testament points to Jesus — producing books that are as enjoyable to read as they are theologically significant.

About the Jesus Moments Series

Jesus Moments: Moses is the second book in the Jesus Moments series — a growing collection of beautifully illustrated Old Testament storybooks that look at how key Old Testament characters and events point to Jesus. The series is built on the conviction that children aged 4 to 7 are never too young to begin seeing the connections between the Testaments — and that the earlier they develop this skill, the richer and more faithful their engagement with Scripture will be for the rest of their lives.

Books in the Jesus Moments series available at forthetruth.in:

  • Jesus Moments: David — Book One
  • Jesus Moments: Moses — Book Two

The Story Moses Was Always Telling

When Jesus walked with two disciples on the road to Emmaus after his resurrection, he did something extraordinary. Beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them what was said in all the Scriptures concerning himself.

He showed them that Moses was never just about Moses. That every burning bush, every Passover lamb, every crossing of the sea, every piece of bread from heaven — all of it was telling a story about him.

Jesus Moments: Moses gives the youngest children in your family or church their first glimpse of that same discovery — the discovery that made the disciples' hearts burn within them on the road to Emmaus, and that has the power to transform the way your child reads the Bible for the rest of their life.

name: Bible Stories Every Child Should Know
description:
Bible Stories Every Child Should Know — More Than 120 Stories from the Whole Bible

There is a particular quality to a story told well by someone who loves both the story and the listener.

It is warm without being sentimental. It is clear without being simplistic. It takes the listener seriously enough to give them the real story — with all its drama and its depth — while loving them enough to tell it in language they can genuinely understand and genuinely enjoy. It sounds less like a lesson being delivered and more like a grandfather settling into his chair with his grandchildren gathered around him, beginning with the words that have always worked: let me tell you a story.

That is exactly the quality that Kenneth Taylor brings to Bible Stories Every Child Should Know — a newly illustrated collection of more than 120 Bible stories drawn from his Classic Bible Storybook, presenting the truths of the whole Bible from Genesis to Revelation in the warm, faithful, accessible language that has made Taylor one of the most trusted and most beloved names in children's Christian publishing.

A Voice That Children Trust

Kenneth Taylor — the creator of the Living Bible and one of the most significant figures in the history of making Scripture accessible to ordinary readers — had a particular gift for children's storytelling that is immediately recognisable and immediately enjoyable on every page of this collection.

His stories do not talk down to children. They do not oversimplify the narratives or strip away the genuine drama, the genuine difficulty, or the genuine wonder of what Scripture actually records. But they tell those narratives in language that is genuinely accessible to young readers — clear, warm, unhurried, and delivered with the kind of gentle authority that makes children feel they are in safe hands.

The description that has stayed with readers across generations captures it perfectly: the stories sound like they are being told by a kind grandfather to his grandchildren. That quality — the warmth, the unhurried pacing, the genuine love for both the stories and the children who are hearing them — is what makes this collection not just educational but genuinely enjoyable. Children come back to it not because they have to but because they want to.

More Than 120 Stories from the Whole Bible

One of the most significant features of this collection is its extraordinary breadth. With more than 120 Bible stories drawn from both the Old and New Testaments, it gives children a genuinely comprehensive encounter with the whole of Scripture — not just the most famous stories but the full sweep of the biblical narrative from creation to new creation.

Children who work through this collection will encounter:

From the Old Testament: The creation of the world and the garden of Eden. The fall of Adam and Eve. Noah and the flood. The call of Abraham and the covenant. Joseph and his brothers. Moses and the exodus from Egypt. The ten commandments and the wilderness years. Joshua and the promised land. The judges and the kings. David and Goliath. Solomon's wisdom. Elijah and the prophets. Daniel in Babylon. The great prophetic visions. And many more.

From the New Testament: The birth of Jesus. His childhood and his baptism. The calling of the disciples. The Sermon on the Mount. The parables of the kingdom. The miracles of healing and provision. The entry into Jerusalem. The last supper. The arrest, trial, and crucifixion. The resurrection and the appearances. The ascension and Pentecost. The growth of the early church. Paul's missionary journeys. And the vision of the new creation in Revelation.

Together, these stories give children not just individual narratives but an understanding of the whole sweep of God's story — how each story connects to the ones before and after it, and how all of them together tell the one great story of God's love for his world and his determination to rescue it through Jesus Christ.

Comprehension Questions for Deeper Engagement

One of the features that makes Bible Stories Every Child Should Know particularly valuable as a family devotional resource is the inclusion of 3 or 4 comprehension questions at the end of each story.

These questions are not merely checking whether children have paid attention. They are carefully designed to:

  • Reinforce the key facts and narrative details of each story in a memorable, conversational way
  • Help children develop their understanding of biblical concepts — connecting the specific story to the larger theological framework of Scripture
  • Provide natural starting points for conversation between parents and children about the deeper meaning and personal significance of what they have just heard
  • Develop the habit of active, reflective engagement with Scripture — asking questions of the text rather than simply receiving it passively

For parents who want story time to be more than just entertainment — who want it to be genuine theological formation — these questions make every reading session a genuine learning opportunity.

What This Book Will Help Your Child Do

  • Encounter more than 120 Bible stories from the whole of Scripture — gaining a genuinely comprehensive understanding of the biblical narrative from creation to new creation
  • Develop a genuine love for the stories of the Bible — through the warm, accessible, grandfather-quality storytelling that makes every narrative genuinely enjoyable
  • Build a whole-Bible framework for understanding God, humanity, sin, salvation, and the hope of the new creation
  • Develop the habit of asking and answering questions about what they have heard — building comprehension, theological vocabulary, and genuine engagement with the meaning of each story
  • Experience the Bible as a unified, coherent, personally relevant narrative rather than a disconnected collection of individual stories
  • Lay the deep biblical foundations that will undergird their faith, their character, and their understanding of the world for the rest of their lives

Who Should Use This Book?

Bible Stories Every Child Should Know is ideal for:

  • Parents wanting a comprehensive, high-quality, whole-Bible children's storybook that will give their children a genuine encounter with the full scope of Scripture
  • Families wanting a family devotional resource that works for multiple ages simultaneously — from young children to grandparents — bringing generations together around the stories of God's Word
  • Grandparents wanting to give a meaningful, multi-generational gift that will both introduce grandchildren to the Bible and connect them to a tradition of storytelling that shaped their own faith
  • Sunday school teachers and children's ministry workers wanting a comprehensive Bible story resource with built-in comprehension questions for teaching and discussion
  • Home-educating families wanting to incorporate a systematic, whole-Bible narrative curriculum into their programme
  • Churches wanting to resource families with the most comprehensive, most faithfully told, and most warmly accessible children's Bible story collection available
  • Any family in India wanting to give their children a genuine, comprehensive, warmly told introduction to the whole of Scripture — from the trusted voice of one of Christian publishing's most beloved storytellers

About the Author

description:
A Very Noisy Christmas — A Fun and Joyful Retelling of the Christmas Story

We often think of the first Christmas as a silent night.

Peaceful. Quiet. A gentle baby sleeping in a manger while angels hover softly overhead and shepherds tiptoe reverently through the darkness.

But what if the first Christmas was actually a great deal noisier than that?

What if it was filled with the sound of angels shouting with joy, shepherds running and calling out to one another, a baby crying in a stable, and the whole creation breaking into the kind of noise that only the most extraordinary news in the history of the universe could produce?

A Very Noisy Christmas is a wonderfully fun, genuinely interactive, and joyfully energetic retelling of the Christmas story for children aged 2 to 4 — one that invites young children not just to listen but to join in. To make noise. To shout and sing and respond to the most exciting birth announcement the world has ever heard with the kind of whole-body, unselfconscious, utterly delightful noise that only very young children can produce with complete abandon.

This is Christmas as it was always meant to be celebrated — not in hushed reverence alone, but with the joyful, exuberant, thoroughly noisy enthusiasm that the arrival of God's Son into the world genuinely deserves.

Beyond Silent Night

The association of Christmas with silence and peacefulness is beautiful — and not entirely wrong. There is genuine wonder and genuine stillness in the nativity scene. The intimacy of a mother and her newborn child. The quiet of a stable late at night.

But the Bible's account of the first Christmas is also full of noise. The angels did not whisper their announcement to the shepherds — they proclaimed it with the kind of glory that left those shepherds terrified before they were overjoyed. The shepherds did not quietly make their way to Bethlehem — they hurried, and when they had seen the baby they went out and told everyone they met what they had heard and seen. Mary sang. Zechariah prophesied. Simeon broke into praise. Anna gave thanks to God loudly enough for everyone in the temple to hear.

The first Christmas was a noisy event. And A Very Noisy Christmas captures that noise — and invites the youngest children to add their own voices to it.

An Interactive Story for the Very Young

What makes A Very Noisy Christmas particularly special for children aged 2 to 4 is its regular invitations to make noise — built into the text at natural moments throughout the story, inviting children to respond to what they are hearing with their voices, their bodies, and their whole enthusiastic selves.

This interactivity is not just fun — though it is genuinely, delightfully fun. It is also genuinely effective as a way of helping very young children engage with and remember the story they are hearing. Children at this age learn through participation. They learn through movement and sound and response. A story that invites them in — that gives them a role to play, a sound to make, a response to offer — is a story they engage with far more deeply than one they simply observe.

By the time the story is finished, children who have made noise throughout it will have participated in the Christmas story in a way that makes it genuinely their own — a story they were part of, not just a story they heard.

The Profound Message at the Heart of the Noise

For all its fun and its noise, A Very Noisy Christmas carries a genuinely profound message at its centre — the message that is the reason for all the noise in the first place:

The birth of God's Son, Jesus, who came to make a friendship with God possible for everyone.

This is the truth that made the angels shout. This is the truth that sent the shepherds running. This is the truth that has been making noise across twenty centuries of Christmas celebrations and that gives every child who hears this story their own reason to join in.

Not just a baby in a manger. Not just a warm seasonal story. But the arrival of the Son of God into the world — the moment when heaven came to earth, when God became a child, when the friendship between God and human beings that sin had broken was opened up again through the one who came to restore it.

That is the noise A Very Noisy Christmas is making. And it invites every child who hears it to make that noise too.

  • Experience Christmas not just as a seasonal event but as the most exciting news that has ever been announced — news worth making noise about

  • Families wanting a Christmas read-aloud tradition that is joyful, energetic, and genuinely engaging for the very youngest members of the household

  • Sunday school teachers and children's ministry workers wanting a noisy, interactive Christmas resource for toddler groups and preschool Christmas events
  • Churches planning Christmas family services, toddler nativity events, or festive outreach and wanting a resource that gets the very youngest children actively participating in the Christmas story
  • Toddler groups and parent and child groups wanting a fun, Christmas-themed read-aloud resource that is appropriate for children of mixed backgrounds while centring on the real meaning of Christmas

A Perfect Christmas Gift

A Very Noisy Christmas is specifically identified as a wonderful gift or stocking stuffer for children aged 2 to 4 — and it is easy to see why. It is:

  • The right size and the right format for young children to hold and engage with
  • Beautifully illustrated and visually engaging for the youngest readers
  • Interactive enough to hold a toddler's attention from beginning to end
  • Theologically faithful enough to give parents genuine confidence in what it is communicating
  • Fun enough to be read again and again — which is exactly what toddlers will want to do

Whether given as a Christmas gift to a young child in your own family, shared with a toddler group, distributed at a church Christmas event, or used in a Sunday school nativity activity — A Very Noisy Christmas is a resource that serves beautifully in every context.

About the Very Best Bible Stories Series

A Very Noisy Christmas is part of the Very Best Bible Stories series — a collection of Bible storybooks designed to bring the stories of Scripture to life for the very youngest children in an accessible, engaging, and genuinely faith-forming way. Each title in the series is crafted with the same commitment to both genuine enjoyment and genuine theological faithfulness that characterises A Very Noisy Christmas.

Make Some Noise

The angels made noise. The shepherds made noise. The whole heavenly host broke into the kind of praise that shook the night sky over Bethlehem with the sound of the best news the world had ever heard.

Christmas is a noisy event. It always was. And A Very Noisy Christmas is an invitation to every young child — and every parent who reads it with them — to add their own voices to the noise that has been going on ever since that first extraordinary night.

Because the arrival of God's Son is worth making noise about. Now. Always. Together.

name: God's Big Promises Bible Storybook
description:
God's Big Promises Bible Storybook — 92 Stories of the God Who Always Keeps His Word

From the very first pages of Scripture to the very last, one truth runs through every story, every character, every turn of the narrative, every moment of triumph and every moment of failure:

God makes promises. And God keeps them.

He promised to send a rescuer when everything first went wrong in the garden. He promised Abraham a son and a people and a land when Abraham had none of these things. He promised David a king from his line whose throne would last forever. He promised his people a new heart and a new covenant and a new creation. And he kept every promise — in the person of Jesus Christ, who is himself the yes and amen to every promise God has ever made.

That is the one big story of the Bible. And God's Big Promises Bible Storybook is a beautifully illustrated, faithfully told, and genuinely gospel-centred introduction to that story for children aged 2 to 6 — spanning over 400 pages of warmly illustrated narrative, 92 carefully selected Bible stories from both the Old and New Testaments, and five promise themes that run through the whole collection, helping even the youngest children begin to see the Bible not as a collection of disconnected tales but as one unified story about the God who always keeps his word.

92 Stories — One Big Promise

The most important thing to understand about God's Big Promises Bible Storybook is not the number of stories it contains — impressive as 92 stories across 400 pages is for a children's Bible in this age range. It is the way those stories are connected.

Most children's Bibles present Bible stories as individual, self-contained narratives — each with its own lesson, its own moral, its own application, standing more or less independently of the stories around it. This approach has its merits. But it misses the most important thing about the Bible: that it is one story, not many. That every individual narrative — from Noah and the Ark to the parable of the prodigal son — is a chapter in a single, unified, brilliantly coherent narrative that moves from creation through fall through redemption to new creation, with the promises of God as the thread that holds it all together.

God's Big Promises Bible Storybook is built on exactly this understanding. The 92 stories are not presented as independent moral tales. They are woven together to reveal the overarching narrative of Scripture — God's unwavering commitment to redeem his people, expressed through a series of promises that build on one another, that point forward to their fulfilment in Christ, and that together constitute the most extraordinary story of love and faithfulness that has ever been told.

Children who grow up with this book are being given something far more valuable than a collection of Bible facts. They are being given a framework — a whole-Bible understanding of what God is doing in the world — that will serve them for a lifetime of Scripture reading and Christian living.

The Five Promise Themes

One of the most distinctive and most practically useful features of God's Big Promises Bible Storybook is its use of five promise themes — identified by bright, visually distinctive icons throughout the book — that help children track the running threads of God's promises across the whole of the biblical narrative.

These five themes are not artificial categories imposed on the text from outside. They are the genuine, biblically groted promise-threads that run through Scripture itself — the recurring patterns of divine commitment that build across the Testaments and find their ultimate fulfilment in Christ:

The Promise of a Rescuer From the very first promise in Genesis 3 — the seed of the woman who will crush the serpent's head — through the great messianic prophecies of the Old Testament, to the arrival of Jesus in the New Testament, the promise of a rescuer runs through the whole of the biblical narrative as its central, animating hope. Every time children see this icon, they are being reminded that every story is part of the story of the one who was always coming.

The Promise of a People God's promise to Abraham — that he would make him the father of a great nation through whom all the families of the earth would be blessed — is one of the most foundational promises in all of Scripture. It is fulfilled not just in the nation of Israel but in the church — the community gathered from every nation and tribe and tongue who are the true children of Abraham by faith in Christ. Children who track this theme across the Bible's stories are developing an understanding of the church as the fulfilment of God's ancient covenant purposes.

The Promise of a Place The land promise to Abraham, the promised land of Canaan, the temple as the place where God dwells with his people, the new Jerusalem of Revelation — the promise of a place where God and his people will dwell together runs through the whole of Scripture and finds its ultimate fulfilment in the new creation. Children who track this theme are developing an eschatological hope — an understanding of where the whole story is going — from the very earliest years.

The Promise of Blessing God's promise of blessing — the commitment to do good to his people, to provide for them, to care for them, to make his face shine upon them — runs through every covenant and every story of the Bible. Children who track this theme are developing a deep, personal sense of the goodness and the generosity of the God who keeps his promises.

The Promise of God's Presence Perhaps the most personally significant of the five themes — the promise that God himself will be with his people, that he will not abandon them, that he will walk with them through every difficulty and every darkness — runs from the garden through the tabernacle through the incarnation through the gift of the Spirit through the new creation, where God himself will dwell with his people and be their God forever.

Familiar Tales and Lesser-Known Stories

One of the great strengths of God's Big Promises Bible Storybook is its willingness to go beyond the handful of most familiar Bible stories that dominate most children's Bibles — while still including the beloved classics that every child should know.

Children will encounter the familiar stories they love: Noah and the Ark, the story of Moses and the exodus, David and Goliath, the birth of Jesus, the feeding of the five thousand, the resurrection. These stories are told with the warmth, the faithfulness, and the clarity that children need and deserve.

But they will also encounter stories they may never have heard before — stories like Jacob and Esau, Rahab and the spies, the calling of Samuel, the story of Naomi and Ruth, the ministry of Elisha, the return of the exiles from Babylon. These lesser-known stories are not footnotes to the biblical narrative — they are essential chapters in the one big story that God is telling. And children who know them have a richer, more complete, more genuinely biblical understanding of what that story is than children who know only the most commonly told accounts.

Together, the familiar and the unfamiliar stories create a genuinely comprehensive encounter with the whole of Scripture — one that gives children the full sweep of the biblical narrative rather than a highlights reel of its most dramatic moments.

What This Book Will Help Your Child Do

  • Encounter 92 faithfully told Bible stories from both the Old and New Testaments — gaining a genuinely comprehensive introduction to the whole of Scripture from the earliest years
  • Begin to understand the Bible as one unified story — not a collection of disconnected tales but a single, coherent narrative about the God who makes and keeps his promises
  • Track five promise themes across the whole biblical narrative — developing an understanding of the running threads of God's covenant faithfulness that connects every story to every other
  • Encounter both familiar beloved stories and lesser-known biblical narratives — building a genuinely comprehensive biblical knowledge rather than just a highlights reel
  • Develop a genuine, early love for God's Word — through beautifully illustrated stories told with faithfulness, warmth, and the kind of narrative engagement that makes children want to come back for more
  • Begin to know the promise-keeping God who loves them — developing from the earliest years a personal, trusting, relationship-rooted faith in the God whose word is always reliable

Who Should Use This Book?

God's Big Promises Bible Storybook is ideal for:

  • Parents of children aged 2 to 6 wanting to introduce their children to the Bible in a way that is both comprehensively faithful and genuinely engaging for the very youngest readers
  • Families wanting a whole-Bible children's storybook that presents the complete sweep of the biblical narrative rather than a selection of the most famous stories
  • Grandparents looking for a meaningful, faith-forming, beautifully illustrated gift that will introduce grandchildren to the promise-keeping God who loves them
  • Sunday school teachers and children's ministry workers wanting a high-quality, theologically sound, and comprehensively covering children's Bible storybook for use in teaching or as a class gift
  • Home-educating families wanting to incorporate a systematic, whole-Bible narrative into their curriculum through beautifully crafted, age-appropriate children's literature
  • Churches wanting to resource families with the most faithful, most comprehensive, and most beautifully illustrated children's Bible storybook available for the 2-6 age group
  • Any family in India wanting to give their young children a genuinely comprehensive, warmly illustrated introduction to the whole of God's Word — and to the promise-keeping God who stands behind every story it tells

A Trusted Starting Point for a Lifelong Love

The years from 2 to 6 are among the most formative in a child's entire life. The stories they hear in those years, the images that shape their imagination, the foundational convictions that begin to form in their earliest understanding of the world — all of these leave impressions that are extraordinarily deep and extraordinarily durable.

God's Big Promises Bible Storybook is designed to make the most of those years — to plant in young hearts and minds the seeds of a genuine, whole-Bible, promise-rooted understanding of the God who made them and loves them, that will grow and deepen and bear fruit across an entire lifetime of Christian faith and Christian living.

It is, in the best possible sense, a trusted starting point. Not the end of a child's encounter with Scripture — but the beginning of a love for God's Word that, once planted in these earliest years, has the potential to shape everything that follows.

name: Love Came Down at Christmas
description:
The World Knows the Word. This Book Explains the Reality.

Every year, without fail, the word love fills the Christmas season. It is in the carols piped through shopping centres and the messages scrawled on gift tags. It is in the adverts and the greetings cards, the sentimental films and the festive wishes. Everyone, it seems, agrees: Christmas is about love.

But what does that actually mean?

Because if love really did come down at Christmas — if the birth of Jesus Christ was the most extraordinary act of love in the history of the universe — then surely it deserves more than a few lines on a card. Surely it deserves to be looked at closely, carefully, and with wonder.

That is exactly what Love Came Down at Christmas invites you to do.

What This Devotional Is

Written by one of the most respected Reformed theologians of our generation, Love Came Down at Christmas is a 24-day Advent devotional that takes an unexpected and deeply rewarding approach to the Christmas season: it opens 1 Corinthians 13 — the great love chapter of the Bible — and reads it in the light of the incarnation.

Sinclair B. Ferguson, with his trademark blend of theological depth and pastoral warmth, unfolds the famous characteristics of love from that chapter — patient, kind, not envious, not self-seeking — and asks: what did this look like in the life of Jesus Christ? And what might it look like in yours?

The result is a devotional that is both intellectually satisfying and personally searching. It will deepen your understanding of the incarnation, renew your wonder at the love of God, and quietly challenge you to love as Christ loved.

How the Devotional Works

Each of the 24 daily readings is built around a passage from 1 Corinthians 13, read through the lens of Christ's life and the miracle of His coming. Ferguson moves through the chapter with the care of a skilled expositor and the heart of a faithful pastor, never letting the theology float free of its personal application.

Every reading concludes with:

  • A question for personal reflection — honest, searching, and grounded in Scripture
  • A prayer — giving words to the response each reading calls for

Whether read alone in the early morning quiet, shared as a couple, or used as a family Advent resource, the structure is simple enough for any reader to follow and rich enough to reward careful attention day after day.

About the Approach: 1 Corinthians 13 Meets the Incarnation

The choice to read 1 Corinthians 13 through the Advent season is one of the quiet strokes of genius in this book. Most people know the chapter from weddings — "Love is patient, love is kind." But Ferguson reminds us that this description of love was not written as a formula for romance. It was written to describe the character of God in Christ.

Every attribute of love that Paul lists in that chapter is an attribute that was perfectly displayed in the life of Jesus — from His patience with His disciples to His refusal to seek His own glory, from His bearing of all things at the cross to His hope that never faltered. Reading 1 Corinthians 13 through this lens transforms both the chapter and the Christmas story.

By Christmas Eve, readers will have seen the love of God in Christ with fresh eyes — and will find themselves unable to hear those familiar carols in quite the same way again.

Key Themes Explored in This Book

The Incarnation as the Supreme Act of Love This devotional roots Christmas firmly in theology. The birth of Jesus was not a touching story — it was God entering His own creation in an act of love so costly it defies full comprehension. Ferguson helps readers feel the weight of what Christmas actually means.

Love Defined by Christ, Not Culture In a season when the word "love" is used to sell everything from perfume to holidays, this book reclaims the word's true meaning — not as a sentiment, but as a Person. Jesus Christ is the definition of love, and 1 Corinthians 13 is His biography.

Personal Challenge to Love Like Christ This is not merely a book to read and admire. Each day's reflection turns the lens inward — asking what it looks like to be patient, kind, humble, and self-giving in the ordinary relationships of daily life. What Would It Have Felt Like to Be on the Inside?

We usually watch the Christmas story unfold from the outside looking in, as we see Mary and Joseph, the shepherds, and then the wise men all arrive in Bethlehem. But what would it have looked like to be on the inside? Christian Focus

What if you were Mary — a young girl in a small town, living an ordinary life — and an angel arrived one night to tell you that you were to give birth to the Son of God? What would you feel? What would you think? How would you make sense of it? And how would you hold on when the days that followed brought confusion, vulnerability, and wonder in equal measure?

The Promise and the Light by Katy Morgan is a book that asks these questions — and answers them with imagination, historical care, and deep biblical faithfulness. Written as a series of vivid and dramatic first-person accounts, it tells the stories of Mary, Joseph, and Zechariah as they experience the events of the first Christmas. For children aged 8–12 who love to read, it is the Christmas gift they did not know they were waiting for. Amazon

Step Inside the Story

The nativity is the most retold story in the history of the world. And yet — for all its familiarity — most people have only ever encountered it from the outside. We know what happened. We know the sequence of events. What we rarely stop to imagine is what it actually felt like to be the people it was happening to.

Katy Morgan takes readers on a journey through the perspectives of Joseph, Mary, and Zechariah, reliving the social expectations of ancient life, the unexpected interruptions of heavenly messengers, and the wonder surrounding the birth of the promised Saviour. Christian Focus

Through Mary's eyes, readers feel the disorientation and the awe of the angel's announcement — the world-turning strangeness of being chosen for something no human being has ever been chosen for, and the quiet, profound trust that overcomes the fear.

Through Joseph's eyes, readers feel the confusion of loving someone in an impossible situation — and the grace of a God who speaks even in the middle of the night, into the depths of a broken dream.

Through Zechariah's eyes, readers feel the accumulated longing of a lifetime — the old priest who has prayed for a son and for the Messiah of Israel, and who can barely believe it when the answer to both prayers finally comes.

Fire your imagination with this story full of wonder, amazement, confusion and shock as you look through the eyes of Mary, Joseph and Zechariah at the first Christmas. Amazon

Imaginative — and Biblically Faithful

She imagines the inner lives of people whose outer circumstances the Bible records — and she does so with care, historical research, and a deep reverence for the scriptural text.

Notes at the back highlight the known facts versus the imaginative parts — a feature that makes the book genuinely educational as well as entertaining, helping readers distinguish what the Bible actually says from what the author has imaginatively filled in. Every Child Knows the Waiting. Benjamin Knows It Best.

Advent is a season of waiting. Children feel it acutely — the anticipation that builds through December, the sense that something extraordinary is coming, the question that hangs in the air: when?

Benjamin — the littlest watchman — has been waiting too. But his waiting is different. He is part of a people who have been waiting for centuries — not just for Christmas morning but for the promised Saviour King that God said he would send. And on the night that changes everything, Benjamin is there to see it.

The Littlest Watchman by Scott James is a gripping, beautifully written Advent adventure story for children aged 3–7 that takes readers into the world of the first Christmas through the eyes of an unexpected witness. It is a perfect gift for the Advent season — one that helps children focus on Jesus at Christmas while being completely gripped by the adventure of Benjamin's story.

More Than a Nativity Retelling — A Story With Deep Roots

What sets The Littlest Watchman apart from most Christmas children's books is its theological depth. Scott James does not begin the story on Christmas night — he begins it much earlier, in the long centuries of waiting that preceded the birth of Jesus.

Benjamin is part of a people who have been living in anticipation — shaped by the promises of God, watching for the Saviour King who was coming. His story gives children a sense of the full biblical context of Christmas: why God's people were waiting, what they were waiting for, and why the birth of Jesus was not just a wonderful surprise but the fulfilment of promises that God had been making for thousands of years.

This Advent perspective — Christmas as the culmination of a long story of promise and anticipation — is one of the most important things a Christian child can grasp about the season. And The Littlest Watchman communicates it through narrative rather than through explanation, which means children absorb it naturally, through the excitement of Benjamin's adventure rather than through a theology lesson.

Gripped by the Nativity — All Over Again

One of the greatest challenges of Christmas children's books is freshness. Most children who grow up in Christian families have heard the nativity story many times — and familiarity can dull the sense of wonder that the story deserves to generate. The angels, the shepherds, the manger — these can become background scenery rather than astonishing events.

The Littlest Watchman addresses this directly by telling the nativity from an unfamiliar perspective — through the eyes of Benjamin, who encounters the events of the first Christmas as a participant rather than an observer. His adventure draws children into the story in a new way, making them feel the anticipation, the wonder, and the joy of the first Christmas as though they are experiencing it for the first time.

As the book's own description puts it: kids will be gripped by what Benjamin saw and will be excited by the nativity story all over again.

The Littlest Watchman is designed specifically as an Advent resource — a book to be read in the weeks leading up to Christmas as part of a family's intentional preparation for the season. Its focus on waiting, promise, and fulfilment makes it an ideal companion for the Advent period, helping children understand why the season is not just a countdown to presents but a season of profound spiritual anticipation.

The book can also be paired with an accompanying Jesse Tree Advent calendar for family Advent devotions — a calendar that takes families through the Old Testament promises and prophecies that point forward to Jesus, connecting the waiting of God's people across the centuries to the waiting of Advent today. Together, the book and the Jesse Tree calendar form one of the most complete and theologically rich Advent resources available for Christian families with young children.

description:
Christmas Is Supposed to Be About Joy. What Happened?

Most of us have felt it — the peculiar gap between what Christmas is supposed to be and what it so often becomes. The season that promises joy and peace arrives with pressure and exhaustion. The time that is meant to draw families together can find them arguing by Boxing Day. The celebration that is supposed to be about the most extraordinary gift ever given can become overwhelmed by the noise, the expense, and the busyness of everything surrounding it.

Something needs to change. Not in the external circumstances of Christmas — but in the hearts of those who celebrate it.

The One True Gift by Tim Chester is an Advent devotional for exactly this need. Twenty-four short daily readings — one for each day of December leading to Christmas — that peel back the layers of the season and bring readers back to the person at its centre: the Lord Jesus, the one true gift that God has given to the world. These are readings designed not merely to inform but to transform — to prepare the heart, kindle genuine joy, and send the reader into Christmas Day as a bearer of peace and goodwill rather than a carrier of the season's accumulated stress and distraction.

Peeling Back the Layers

The description of this devotional uses a phrase that captures its whole purpose: Tim Chester peels back the layers of Christmas. This is what good Advent reflection does — it strips away the accumulated additions, cultural overlays, commercial pressure, and sentimental familiarity that can obscure the extraordinary reality at the heart of the season, and it brings the reader back to what Christmas actually is.

What Christmas actually is, is the incarnation of the eternal Son of God. The moment when the one through whom all things were created took on human flesh. The night when the angels sang and the shepherds ran and the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. This is the event — this specific, historical, world-changing event — that Christmas exists to celebrate. And when Christians encounter it freshly, clearly, and with open hearts, it produces exactly the joy and peace that the season promises.

Chester is one of the most gifted biblical communicators writing today — and his particular skill is making the deep things of the gospel clear, fresh, and personally transforming for ordinary readers. In The One True Gift, he brings that skill to bear on the Advent season — helping readers encounter Christ afresh in a way that reorients everything about how they experience and celebrate Christmas.

Twenty-Four Readings — Each Complete in Itself

Each of the twenty-four daily readings is designed to be short enough to work in the rhythm of December's busy days — accessible in ten to fifteen minutes — and substantive enough to genuinely shape the heart and mind for the day ahead. Each reading includes:

  • The reading itself — a focused, warm, and Christ-centred reflection on an aspect of the incarnation and its meaning
  • Ideas for reflection — questions and prompts for personal engagement with the material
  • Prayer — guidance for responding to what has been read in prayer
  • Application — practical, honest suggestions for how the day's truth changes how the reader lives and relates in the Advent season

Together these elements make each day not just a reading but a complete Advent devotional experience — moving from text to reflection to prayer to application in a way that forms the whole person rather than just informing the mind.

Hymns, Carols, and Prayers

In addition to the twenty-four daily readings, The One True Gift includes a rich supplement of hymns, carols, and prayers — resources for preparing the heart through the music and poetry that the church has used for centuries to celebrate and meditate on the mystery of the incarnation.

This feature makes the devotional not just a book of readings but a fuller Advent companion — drawing on the whole tradition of Christian Christmas hymnody and prayer to set the daily reflections in their proper context of worship. For families using the devotional together, these hymns and carols provide a natural way of including the singing that has always been part of the church's Advent preparation.

A Devotional for Every Kind of Reader

The One True Gift is written for the full range of Christians who want to prepare their hearts for Christmas:

For the busy parent who barely has time to breathe in December but knows that something intentional needs to happen to keep Christmas centred on Christ — these short, complete, practically applied readings are exactly the right length and format.

For the long-time Christian who knows the Christmas story well but finds that familiarity has dulled its wonder — Chester's fresh, layer-peeling engagement with the incarnation offers the kind of renewed encounter with Christ that the most familiar truths sometimes need.

For the small group or family wanting to use Advent readings together — the hymns, carols, prayers, and reflection questions make the devotional naturally shareable and discussion-generating.

For the pastor or church leader who wants to prepare their own heart before helping others prepare theirs — Chester's theological depth and pastoral warmth make this exactly the kind of personal resource that sustains the one who is called to sustain others.

name: There's a Lion in My Nativity!
description:
Mary Thinks She's the Star. She's About to Find Out She Isn't.

The costumes are ready. The lines have been learned. The nativity play is about to begin. And Mary — in her very important role, in her very important costume — is absolutely certain of one thing: she is the star of the show.

But something is going wrong.

One by one, unexpected characters and objects are stealing every scene. A tent. A phone. And — most puzzling of all — a lion.

What on earth is a lion doing in the nativity?

There's a Lion in My Nativity! by Lizzie Laferton is a joyful, witty, warmly illustrated, and genuinely gospel-rich Christmas picture book for children aged 4–7 — the kind of book that makes children laugh and then makes them think, and leaves them understanding something true and wonderful about why Jesus came. It is the perfect Christmas gift for young readers, and one that parents and grandparents will find themselves enjoying every bit as much as the children they read it with.

The Scene-Stealer Who Teaches the Deepest Truths

What makes this book so distinctive and so delightful is its playful structure. As Mary watches each scene of the nativity play get hijacked by an unlikely intruder, she is baffled and increasingly frustrated. But with the help of the narrator, she — and the young reader alongside her — gradually discovers that each unexpected element is actually teaching something profound about who Jesus is and why he came:

The tent — at first glance just a bizarre prop that doesn't belong — turns out to be a picture of the incarnation itself. Jesus did not come to dwell in palaces or cathedrals. He came to pitch his tent among us — to live with us humbly, in the ordinary messiness of human life.

The phone — modern, incongruous, and apparently completely out of place in a first-century Bethlehem scene — turns out to be a picture of connection. Jesus came to reconnect us to God — to bridge the gap that sin had made, to restore the communication that had been broken.

The lion — the most surprising intruder of all — turns out to be the most important. Because Jesus is not just a baby in a manger. He is the King of the universe. The Lion of the tribe of Judah. The one before whom every knee will bow. The nativity is not the whole story — it is the beginning of the story of the King who came in humble disguise, and who will one day be revealed in all his glory.

By the end, Mary has understood — and so has the reader. Jesus is the true star of the show. Not because he stole anyone else's spotlight, but because he is the one the whole story is about.

Rhyme, Warmth, and Genuine Gospel Depth

Lizzie Laferton writes in rhyme — and she does it with the skill and energy of someone who understands that the best children's books are not dumbed-down lessons but genuinely enjoyable literary experiences. The rhymes are clever, the rhythm carries the reader through the story with momentum, and the humour is warm and genuinely funny — the kind that works for children and adults in the room at the same time.

Kim Barnes's illustrations bring the story to life with a distinctive quirky warmth that perfectly matches the tone of Lizzie's writing. The images are bright, expressive, and full of the kind of visual humour that children will pore over on every reread — finding new things they missed the first time through.

A Christmas Book That Actually Explains Christmas

One of the most significant things that can be said about There's a Lion in My Nativity! is that it does what relatively few Christmas picture books for children actually do: it explains, clearly and memorably, what the incarnation actually means.

The tent, the phone, and the lion are not merely comic devices. They are theological images — unexpected and initially puzzling, but ultimately illuminating pictures of the humility, the reconciling work, and the kingly identity of Jesus. Children who work through this book with a parent or grandparent are not just enjoying a funny story about a nativity play. They are encountering real, substantive, gospel truth — presented in a way that they can grasp, feel, and remember.

This is the kind of Christmas resource that a church in India can give away at a Christmas event, a family can read every year as part of their Christmas traditions, and a grandparent can give to a grandchild knowing that it will still be treasured and meaningful a decade later.

  • The tent — a picture of the incarnation and the humility of God coming to live among us
  • The phone — a picture of Jesus as the one who reconnects us to God
  • The lion — a picture of Jesus as the King of the universe, the Lion of Judah
  • The central truth: Jesus is the true star of Christmas — and knowing him is the most wonderful thing of all

name: Is Christmas Unbelievable?
description:
Most People Think the Christmas Story Is a Fantasy. Here Is the Evidence That It Is Not.

Every year, billions of people celebrate Christmas. And every year, a growing number of people assume that the story at the heart of it — a virgin giving birth in Bethlehem, angels announcing the news to shepherds, wise men following a star — is simply a beautiful myth. A lovely story for children. A fairy tale dressed up in religious clothes. Not something a rational, educated person in the twenty-first century could actually believe.

Rebecca McLaughlin respectfully but confidently disagrees.

In Is Christmas Unbelievable?, this respected apologist and Cambridge PhD draws on her deep knowledge of history, philosophy, and biblical scholarship to outline the evidence that Jesus was a real person — that the Bible's accounts of his life are historically reliable, and that believing in a virgin birth is not as intellectually ridiculous as it might sound to modern ears.

This is a concise, accessible, and genuinely compelling book that shows there is a rational basis for the belief that the world's most famous story is fact, not fantasy — and how those events in history can infuse our lives today with meaning and joy that no other story can offer.

What This Book Covers

Rebecca McLaughlin works through the key questions and objections surrounding the Christmas story with historical care and apologetic confidence:

  • Was Jesus a real person? — The historical evidence for Jesus' existence — from biblical and non-biblical sources — and why the question is not as open as many assume
  • Is the Bible reliable? — A clear, accessible account of why the Bible's accounts of Jesus' life are historically credible — and what the evidence actually shows
  • Is the virgin birth believable? — A careful, honest engagement with one of the most commonly dismissed aspects of the Christmas story — and why believing it is more rational than many people think
  • What the Christmas story actually claims — What the Gospel accounts of Jesus' birth actually say — and how they hold up to historical scrutiny
  • Fact or fantasy? — The rational basis for believing that the events of the first Christmas really happened — and why that matters
  • Christmas and meaning today — How the historical reality of the Christmas story infuses everyday life with meaning, purpose, and joy that no invented story could ever provide

What Readers Will Learn

  • Why the question of whether Jesus was a real historical person is not as open as popular culture often assumes
  • What the historical evidence for the reliability of the Bible's accounts of Jesus' life actually shows
  • Why believing in the virgin birth is not intellectually absurd — and what the evidence and the argument actually look like
  • How the Christmas story holds up to historical scrutiny — and why it deserves to be taken seriously as history, not dismissed as myth
  • Why the historical reality of Christmas makes all the difference — giving life a meaning, depth, and joy that no invented story ever could
  • How to engage confidently and graciously with friends, family, and colleagues who assume the Christmas story is fantasy
  • Why the world's most famous story is not only believable but life-transforming for those who receive it as true

How to Use This Book

Is Christmas Unbelievable? is concise, compelling, and immediately usable:

  • Personal reading — Ideal for any Christian wanting to understand the historical and apologetic case for the Christmas story — and to engage more confidently with those who dismiss it
  • Evangelistic gift — A warm, intellectually credible, and accessible gift for a sceptical or curious friend or family member at Christmas — short enough to read in one sitting, compelling enough to stay with them

With the promise, it is the turning point of all of history — the moment when everything God had been working toward from the very beginning finally, gloriously, arrived.

This theological depth is woven into the book with a lightness and warmth that young children can grasp and feel, even before they can fully articulate it. A rescuing King — the one who came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many

About the Author and Artist

Alex Webb-Peploe is the creator of Light in the Darkness and the graphic novel series from The Good Book Company. His approach reflects a deep conviction that the stories of Scripture, told faithfully and visually compellingly, have the power to reach audiences that conventional Christian publishing rarely reaches.

About the Series

Together they form a visually cohesive pair that takes readers from the birth of Jesus to his death and resurrection — the whole arc of the gospel story, told in a format that reaches a new and often unreached audience.
